full_judgment:
Mr. Shahidul Islam, J.: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27.3.1995 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong, in Other Class Appeal No. 335 of 1989 allowing the appeal and directing the District Registrar to make an enquiry under Section 74 of the Registration Act and for doing necessary act for getting registered the deed in question on reversing the judgment and decree dated 13.5.1989 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Sadar, Chittagong, in Other Class Suit No. 264 of 1988. 

 4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Sadar, Chittagong by the judgment and decree dated 13.5.1989 dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiff failed to prove due execution of the deed by adducing reliable witnesses. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree the plaintiff preferred Other Class Appeal No. 335 of 1989 and the said appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong, who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 27.3.1995 allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment of the trial Court and directed the concerned District Registrar for holding an enquiry under Section 74 of the Registration Act and for getting registered the deed in question. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree the defendant has obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate for the Petitioner submitted that the scope of investigation by a civil Court under Section 77 of the Registration Act is to find out due execution of the deed in question by the executant and after being satisfied due execution the Court can direct the Sub-Registrar for registration of the deed within 30(thirty) days. He submitted that there is no scope for directing the Registrar for holding any further enquiry under section 74 of the Registration Act after a case was disposed of under section 77 of the Registration Act by a competent civil Court. He submitted that the plaintiff has totally failed to prove due execution of the deed in question by adding any evidence and the trial Court lawfully dismissed the plaintiffs suit holding that the plaintiff has failed to prove due execution. He submitted that the Court of Appeal was concerned only with the question of due execution of the deed in question and the appellate Court had no jurisdiction to direct the concerned Registrar for making any further enquiry. He submitted that by the judgment and decree the Court of appeal has directed the concerned District Registrar to investigate into the question of due execution under section 74 of the Registration Act which is beyond his jurisdiction. He submitted that the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law and is liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions Mr. Mahmudul Islam cited the case law reported in 37 DLR(AD) 190. 5 BCR (AD) 119. He further submitted that the question of due execution having not been proved and the plaintiff having failed to take any steps for proving due execution this Court in exercising of ' its revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not entitled to send the suit back on remand to the trial Court for fresh investigation. In support of his submissions he relied upon the case law reported in 54 DLR (AD) 74 and 53 DLR (AD) 1 10. He prayed for an interference of this Court as against the judgment and decree impugned in this Rule. 

 11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 27.3.1995 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong, in Other Class Appeal No. 335 of 1989 allowing the appeal and directing the District Registrar to make an enquiry under Section 74 of the Registration Act and for taking necessary act for getting registered the deed in question is set aside. The judgment and decree dated 13.5.1989 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Sadar, Chittagong, in Other Class Suit No. 264 of 1988 is hereby restored. The order of stay granted by this Court dated 15.5.1995 is hereby vacated.
